vault.//: Assembles the site's vault, dist/vault, from its sources: content/public, then the private notes' stubs in dist/vault-private, each at the vault's root (src/lib/assembly.ts). Notes are copied, with each link's public/ or private/ prefix (Obsidian's, from content/) taken off and each tags/<tag>/index link written tags/<tag> (src/lib/link-prefixes.ts), and attachments linked; what git ignores, and dotfiles, are left out; a source that isn't there is empty; a path in both sources fails it, naming both files. dist/vault/.sources.json names each file's source, for its git dates. Never cached: it takes a fraction of a second, and the cache would keep its links as copies.

dev.//: Astro's dev server over the assembled vault, dist/vault. First the tasks git:commit runs before a commit (vault:precommit: the private notes' stubs published, then checked), then the vault assembled from them and its mirrors and slices saved (`mirrors`, which downloads only documents with no mirror yet, so a run after the first stays offline), then the server, with its content cache cleared (`--force`): the cache keeps each note as it was rendered, and a changed Markdown plugin would otherwise show only in notes edited since. The vault's sources are watched, and the vault assembled and read again whenever a file in one changes, so a new or renamed note's links follow without a restart. Its discussion is made up, by `mock-mentions`, a file for each source of it: its webmentions read from WEBMENTIONS_FILE, never webmention.io's; its Bluesky posts from BLUESKY_POSTS_FILE, never Bluesky's; its Hacker News thread from HACKER_NEWS_FILE, never Hacker News's.

options.command: pnpm run vault && pnpm run dev --force

build.//: Build the assembled vault into astro/dist, once `check` passes and `vault` has assembled it: astro build strips types without checking them. The vault and its sources are inputs, so a changed note rebuilds. So is the resume, which `resume:build` compiles into dist/resume and the site publishes (src/lib/resume.ts).

tag-names.//: Read-only: fails when two tags share a name, the last level of each, whatever the case (scripts/check-tag-names.ts): the feed lists a note's tags by name alone, and each nested tag's page is also at /tags/<name> (src/lib/tag-names.ts). First the private notes' stubs published (vault:precommit), then the vault assembled from them. Run by git:commit, so no such vault is committed.

options.command: pnpm run vault && pnpm run tag-names

mock-mentions.//: Writes a made-up discussion for the dev server to show, a file in dist for each source, as its API gives it (scripts/mock-mentions.ts): webmentions (a Bluesky reply by Bridgy among them), the site's Bluesky post of the newest public post, and a Hacker News thread of it; the three newest public posts mentioned, and a note by an alias. First the private notes' stubs published (vault:precommit), then the vault assembled from them, so that a note made private since is never one of them. Run after `vault`, from the notes it assembled; never cached, since which notes are newest changes with the vault.

options.command: pnpm run vault && pnpm run mock-mentions

seo-check.//: Lighthouse, through Unlighthouse, on every page of the sitemap of the site as built, served by `astro preview` on a free port of its own (scripts/seo-check.ts). Prints each category's lowest and mean score and the SEO audits that fail, on which pages; Unlighthouse's report is dist/seo-check/index.html. SEO_CHECK_BUDGET (1-100) fails it when a page scores under the budget in any category; without it, it only reports. Not yet run in CI.

test.//: The unit tests of the pure modules under src/lib, on Vitest, over the fixture vault (test/fixtures/vault). One file: `nx run astro:test -- test/notes.test.ts`.

mirrors.//: Saves a mirror of each annotated document that has none into the mirror directory, the repository's dist/mirrors (MIRRORS_ROOT overrides it), never into the vault; the site serves each under assets/annotated-documents (docs/adr/2801). A saved mirror is pinned and never fetched again; delete it to fetch it afresh. The only target that reaches the network for the vault: run it before a build that should have every mirror, as the deploy does. A document that can't be fetched is reported, and its page is built with its annotations alone. Then recognizes the scanned pages of each mirror with no text file of its own (@chaoticgoodcomputing/pdf-ocr), and keeps their text beside it.

e2e.//: The Playwright specs against the built site: over the fixture vault (src/test/fixture), or with the `vault` configuration over the real one (src/test/vault). The suite builds its own site into .e2e and serves it on a port of its own, which E2E_PORT overrides (docs/adr/0007). One spec: `nx run astro:e2e -- notes`. Never beside another build in the same checkout, and never beside its dev server, which the suite refuses to start next to: every build writes the same .astro directory, and the dev server reads it. Stop the dev server first, or run the suite from another worktree.
